verdict.rationale: Keycloak's own docs say users can manage their sessions in the account console and admins can manage users' sessions in the admin console. The token revocation endpoint adds per-token revocation, but the evidence does not show device listing or explicit individual-versus-bulk session revocation. missing for 10: documented device/session detail views, explicit per-session and revoke-all controls for users and admins, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can let users and admins see active sessions and devices and revoke them individually or all at once

citations.quote: Users can also manage sessions as well as view history for the account.
They can also manage users, including permissions and sessions.
The token revocation endpoint is used to revoke tokens. Both refresh tokens and access tokens are supported by this endpoint.
